episodic.task: volume render mri_woman.raw (MRI) so denser tissue stands out and softer tissue is faint, with readable colors
episodic.dataset_type: raw scalar volume (uint16 little-endian), headerless, MRI modality
episodic.what_worked: Recalled range-relative + cutoff + faint-shell/opaque-core lessons from bonsai/engine and they transferred across modality and dtype. Resolved the headerless layout by inspection: two candidate interpretations fit the byte count, so I picked the one with high adjacent-slice correlation (0.88 vs 0.46) and the plausible 12-bit range. Hard background cutoff killed MRI air/noise so no haze appeared first try. Ghosted the broad soft-tissue band and reserved opacity+warm color for the dense band so interior anatomy (skull, sutures) reads.

semantic.rule: Inspect the data's actual scalar min/max at runtime and place every opacity/color control point as a FRACTION of that measured range, never as a fixed scalar value.

Low scalar values are usually background/noise: hold opacity flat at 0 up to a cutoff fraction (lower it when the low-value background dominates the histogram), then ramp up. This removes the speckle 'haze' that otherwise fogs the render.
Always render then LOOK at the PNG; fix opacity/color before finishing. The first transfer function is rarely right.

To reveal interior structure, give the broad outer/low-mid band very low opacity (ghosted) and reserve high opacity for the dense high-value band, with warm bright color on the dense part and cool dim color on the shell.

For a headerless .raw volume, do not assume dtype/shape. When more than one (dtype, dims) interpretation fits the byte count, pick the one whose adjacent slices are most correlated (coherent anatomy) and whose scalar range is physically plausible (e.g. ~0-4095 => 12-bit). Verify before building the transfer function.

corrective.mistake: Gave low-value voxels nonzero opacity, producing a speckle 'haze' cloud around the subject.
corrective.fix: Raise the background cutoff: keep opacity 0 until the low-value background ends (fraction of the measured range) so only real structure is visible.

corrective.mistake: Assumed density increases monotonically with the semantic part (e.g. pot<branch<leaves), which inverted the colors.
corrective.fix: Do not assume which structure is densest. Inspect value distribution (and spatial/height distribution if needed) to decide which scalar band maps to which part before assigning colors.

corrective.mistake: Let the broad outer/soft-tissue band climb to high opacity, forming a solid shell that hid the interior anatomy the task asked to reveal.
corrective.fix: Keep the broad low/mid band a translucent ghost (single-digit-percent opacity) and only ramp to high opacity in the dense high-value band, so the interior reads through the exterior.
